The North Field, off the northeast coast of Qatar, is the largest natural gas field in the world. It was found in 1971 and is shared with Iran, which calls its side South Pars.

Qatar spent the 1990s building plants at Ras Laffan to cool the gas into liquid so it could be shipped by sea. Exports of liquefied natural gas began in the late 1990s, and Qatar became one of the biggest exporters in the world, selling to Japan, Korea, China, India and Europe.

The gas paid for the Qatar Investment Authority, Al Jazeera and the 2022 World Cup. It also made Qatar one of the richest countries per head, and gave it the means to act on its own in Gulf politics.
